shortened: Lars Schöbitz has been the Open Science Specialist and embedded Data Steward at Global Health Engineering (D-MAVT) since the Chair was founded in July 2021. He supports all group members in RDM, RSE, ORD and the FAIR principles and owns the group's data management strategy. His trainings are hands-on application of RDM workflows that are designed, tested and supported.
rationale: Tightened the opening clause and dropped 'carefully'. No facts removed.

shortened: He leads openwashdata, a community funded through four ETH ORD projects, where the toolchain is tested under research conditions turning unpublished WASH (Water, Sanitation, Hygiene) datasets into published, documented, citable data packages. He also runs meta-analysis of the sector, covering research and UN global monitoring, to baseline current data sharing practice and monitor how it changes.
rationale: Merged the two long sentences and cut the restated purpose clause at the end.

shortened: For this he designed and taught ds4owd (Data Science for openwashdata), an online course that trained more than 150 participants to manage and publish data using R, Git, and GitHub, with weekly student hours, support on real assignments using participants' own data, and a capstone project. His teaching is grounded in hands-on practice rather than slides: participants finish able to point to how they addressed the FAIR principles in their own data.
rationale: Cut the philosophy statement, which restated the preceding sentence twice. Kept the 150 participants and the course design.

shortened: It builds on a 4-ECTS class, "Research Beyond the Lab: Open Science and Research Methods for a Global Engineer", designed and taught with Elizabeth Tilley three times (spring 2022, 2024, 2025), in which D-MAVT students ran a research project, collected their own data, learned R, Git, GitHub, and Quarto, and applied FAIR data management, with all material published as Open Educational Resources.
rationale: Trimmed the framing clause only. All course facts kept.

shortened: Alongside the openwashdata projects funded by the ETH Domain ORD programme (Measure 1), he supported the funded Explore project FAIRqual with the D-USYS Transdisciplinarity Lab, on how ORD practice differs for qualitative researchers and on the data governance questions behind it.
rationale: Cut the trailing training-material clause, which duplicates the OER point in the previous paragraph.

shortened: Lars is a data steward in the ETH Zurich Data Stewardship Network (DSN), hosted by the ETH Library, and holds several roles in the reproducibility and RDM community:
rationale: Dropped the back-reference to the previous subsection, which the reader has just read.

shortened: - Local Node Leader for ETH Zurich in the Swiss Reproducibility Network (SwissRN) since 2025.
rationale: Cut the mission restatement; the network's name carries it.

shortened: - Contributor to the AI Disclosure Working Group of the Global Federation of Reproducibility Networks (GFRN), feeding the reproducibility perspective into the Global Reporting Standard for AI Disclosure in Research (ISC, COPE, STM, GYA).
rationale: Compressed the initiative list to the four bodies.

shortened: - Member of the Expert Sounding Group for the ETH Domain ORD Measure 5 project "Career Paths for Open Research Data Professionals" (2025 to 2026).
rationale: Cut the recruitment justification, which is made again in 2.1.

shortened: The programme is built on a data-package pipeline Lars has developed and used for years: it produces tidy data, README files, data dictionaries, and archived Zenodo releases through the R ecosystem, with curated websites for discovery. The GHE Open Science Team uses it daily, taking raw data through an audit trail of versioned, documented steps to a published FAIR data package with a DOI, a citation file recording each contributor's ORCID, and an entry in the ETH Research Collection.
rationale: Merged the opening sentence into the pipeline description. Every output of the pipeline kept.

shortened: He tracks developments in RDM, FAIR, and ORD, including MLCroissant, data-dict.yaml, and RO-Crate (ETH Node), and has presented this workflow under the title "Plan for tomorrow today" at many venues in the reproducibility and RDM communities.
rationale: Dropped 'cutting-edge', the Hadley Wickham attribution, and the reception claim, which the Board cannot verify.

shortened: His employment at Global Health Engineering is permanent and runs for the full project duration, so the team can evaluate whether the offer continues beyond twelve months with a yearly cohort from ETH Zurich and FAIR Coalition members.
rationale: Joined into one sentence. The permanence point is what the criterion asks for and stays.

shortened: Earlier gitforsci and agentsforsci workshops, supported by the DSN and SwissRN, produced training material this programme reuses and refines. Because much of the training covers agentic AI programming, that material is kept current and feeds the wider conversation on declaring AI use in research.
rationale: Cut the opening claim sentence, which the examples prove on their own.

shortened: The digital research assets are the participants' own datasets, with the code, workflows, and documentation needed to make them FAIR. Each of the fifteen participants brings real data from their own work: tabular, survey, measurement and sensor data, and the qualitative material (interviews and recordings) that raises the hardest sharing questions.
rationale: Merged the middle sentence into the list.

shortened: Agentic AI tools give ETH researchers a second reason to make these assets FAIR. An agent that cleans or reuses a dataset needs the same documentation a human colleague needs, such as a data dictionary stating what each variable means. Researchers who document their data well can hand routine work to an agent and check the result; those who do not, cannot. Agents also produce code and text that reach research outputs, so researchers need a way to declare AI use that shows what they still produced themselves. Participants use these tools on their own data, and the declaration of AI use runs through the whole year (section 2.2).
rationale: Joined the two contrasting sentences and cut the sentence saying the programme treats both as part of FAIR, which the next sentence demonstrates.

shortened: The gap is practical. ETH researchers know the FAIR principles exist but often cannot apply them to their own data, largely because adopting new workflows costs time that data sharing and computational reproducibility are not yet rewarded for. Over twelve months the programme lets researchers adopt a new workflow alongside existing practice and build the arguments for it, using established teaching methods: spaced practice, hands-on activities, and relevance to the learner's own work.
rationale: Compressed the reward-structure explanation and merged the teaching-methods sentence.

shortened: The target community is ETH researchers who already hold, or are moving into, RDM responsibility, drawn from several departments, career stages, and disciplines. This is the professionalisation angle of the ETH Domain Measure 5 work on career paths for open research data professionals: the programme upskills people who already carry RDM responsibility, increasingly doctoral students, and is a route into the embedded data stewardship role Global Health Engineering already practises. The cohort balances postdoctoral researchers and doctoral students, alongside scientific and technical staff carrying RDM responsibility; one or two professors is an aspirational goal, carrying the practice into how a group is led. Participants are selected for a dataset of their own, some coding experience, and curiosity about agentic AI tools. The mixed cohort is the point: it lets the programme treat FAIR data sharing as something that differs by community and data type, and produce recommendations specific to those communities.
rationale: Largest single cut. Removed the beginners contrast, the Measure 5 conditional, and the final restatement of the mixed-cohort rationale.

shortened: The innovation is that participants make their own data FAIR by doing it, with support, across a full year. Most FAIR and RDM training at ETH is delivered as short courses or summer schools that do not touch participants' own data. This programme walks each participant from a raw file to a published, citable data package, then supports them while they apply the same workflow to the rest of their data.
rationale: Cut 'rather than learning the principles in the abstract', which the next sentence states concretely.

shortened: A second innovation runs through the year: the declaration of AI use. As participants apply agentic AI workflows to their own data, the programme treats disclosure as an open question in research integrity and develops practical answers with fifteen real researchers. It asks how researchers show which parts of their work they produced themselves, connecting to Lars's contribution to the GFRN AI Disclosure Working Group. The programme explores provenance trails for AI use, from Git commits that make each AI-assisted change visible and reversible to experimental tools such as re_gent that record which agent step and prompt produced a change.
rationale: Cut the ticking-a-box sentence, which repeats a phrase used in 2.1.

shortened: The applicants' own training is a funded part of the project. Lars Schöbitz and Adriana Clavijo Daza will deepen their skills in agentic AI workflows for data management and in organisational-change methods for embedding open-science practice. The organisational-change workshop, delivered by Greg Wilson (author of "Organisational Change for Open Science"), trains the applicants and the cohort together, and the applicants carry the method into later cohorts and their DSN work.
rationale: Compressed the two-areas construction into one sentence.

shortened: The five workshops, the data-package pipeline, and the supporting materials become a repeatable offering Global Health Engineering can run for further ETH cohorts after the project:
rationale: Cut the announcing sentence; the list that follows is the content.

shortened: - Two four-hour workshops on FAIR data sharing and data management, built on the openwashdata workflow, using each participant's own data, with support hours between sessions.
rationale: Minor tightening.

shortened: Community building runs throughout, as the 2nd call requires. Global Health Engineering will host AI Playground sessions three times per term from spring semester 2027, open to anyone at ETH and to the general public. The playground connects the cohort to the wider research community, their own and beyond ETH. It is a general offering that runs with or without this funding, and taking part is not required of the fifteen. A Matrix (Element) channel, open to every ETH member and to the public, gives live support and links the cohort to that community. Quarterly hands-on team meetings keep participants working between workshops, and 1:1 support from Lars and Adriana is available on request. The cohort itself becomes a cross-department community of practice, as participants read and support each other's data and code.
rationale: Cut the trailing clause on community-specific practice, which 2.2 p12 and 2.5 both make.

shortened: The expected outputs are published FAIR data packages from fifteen ETH researchers, each able to repeat the workflow on their remaining data, and a tested programme ready for the next community. Because participants come from several departments and career stages, the practice spreads into their groups.
rationale: Removed 'by the end of the project', already implied.

shortened: The programme also produces a research output. The fifteen participants are both trainees and a study cohort: over a full year it examines how FAIR data sharing, data security, and the declaration of AI use differ across their disciplines. From this come recommendations on community-specific FAIR practice and on declaring AI use, contributing to the conversation on scientific integrity as AI-assisted workflows reshape research.
rationale: Tightened the closing clause.

shortened: The programme runs over twelve months in four work packages, summarised in the table below.
rationale: Points at the milestone table that replaces the bullet list.

shortened: - WP1, Setup and recruitment (months 1 to 2). Complete the cohort to fifteen, continuing the open call with the FAIR Coalition's backing, collect signed commitments, gather each participant's dataset, data description, and RDM competency baseline, set up the ETH GitLab and GitHub spaces and the Matrix channel, and finalise the workshop schedule. Deliverable: a confirmed cohort and a working programme environment. Lead: Lars Schöbitz.
rationale: Cut 'building on those already recruited before submission', covered by the risk bullet in 2.4.

shortened: - WP4, Consolidation, sustainability, and reporting (months 10 to 12). Publish the final data packages, capture the programme as a reusable offering, feed lessons into the DSN, and report. Deliverables: at least fifteen published FAIR data packages, a documented reusable programme, a DSN contribution, a draft data management strategy for each participant's group, final content and financial reports.
rationale: Removed the duplicated reporting phrase and the redundant lead line, which the roles paragraph states.

shortened: Roles: Lars Schöbitz is corresponding applicant and budget manager and leads WP1, WP2, and WP4. Adriana Clavijo Daza co-delivers WP2 and leads WP3 and the DSN link. Greg Wilson delivers the organisational-change workshop. Tools are ETH-native and transferable: ETH GitLab, GitHub, Zenodo, the ETH Research Collection, Matrix (Element), R, and Anthropic Claude Code.
rationale: Minor tightening.

shortened: The programme builds on proven delivery capability. The Global Health Engineering Open Science Team has already trained more than 150 people to publish open data through ds4owd, and the data-package pipeline and much of the workshop material already exist.
rationale: Cut the feasibility assertion; the evidence follows immediately.

shortened: Early-stage proposals were shared with the ETH Library (Julian Dederke) and SwissRN (Daniel Stekhoven, ETHZ local node), so the approach is known to the relevant stakeholders and does not duplicate existing ETH Library courses.
rationale: Compressed the duplication-risk clause.

shortened: - Recruitment risk: the programme is designed for fifteen participants. At submission seven ETH researchers have expressed interest, recruited through an open call across the Data Stewardship Network, the RSE Network, ETH4D, D-USYS TdLab, and the ETH ORD community. They come from four departments (D-GESS, D-USYS, D-EAPS, D-BAUG) and seven research units: six postdoctoral researchers and one doctoral student, working with measurement and sensor data, surveys, qualitative interview and focus-group material, computational and simulation work, and mixed methods. Mitigation: recruitment continues through WP1, more doctoral students can take senior places if those do not fill, and the FAIR Coalition's reach at ETH can fill remaining places. Interest across four departments within two weeks of an open call suggests demand is not the constraint.
rationale: Second largest cut. Removed the section 2.5 cross-reference and compressed the mitigation into one sentence. All seven participants, four departments, and the data types kept.

shortened: - Drop-out risk: researchers work on unpredictable schedules and availability may change across the year. Mitigation: workshops are recorded so participants can follow the taught elements and exercises later, dates are confirmed early to avoid calendar conflicts, and work between workshops is kept small and manageable, with room for those who want to invest more.
rationale: Compressed each mitigation to a clause.

shortened: - Financial and eligibility risk: the CHF 30,000 participant-place cost must read as workshop-organisation cost, not staff salary, because personnel costs are not eligible. Mitigation: the budget books it under conferences and workshop organisation, with no salary and no subcontracting line. The concept was shared with openscience@sl.ethz.ch early and considered appropriate.
rationale: Cut the parenthetical restating what the cost covers. Fixed "in it's early stages".

shortened: The project gives ETH a repeatable programme that turns researchers' own data into published FAIR data packages, and leaves it available after the funding ends. The new service is a tested, hands-on FAIR-implementation programme Global Health Engineering can run for further ETH communities, distinct from the principle-level training the DSN and the RDM Summer School provide.
rationale: Minor tightening.

shortened: The direct benefit is fifteen published, FAIR, citable data packages from fifteen ETH researchers across several departments, each able to repeat the workflow on the rest of their data and pass it to their group. Because the cohort is mixed by discipline and method, the programme produces a case study of how FAIR data sharing, data security, and the declaration of AI use differ between communities. All teaching material is published as Open Educational Resources, with handbooks on delivering it.
rationale: Removed the repeated 'fifteen researchers who' construction.

shortened: Institutional responsibility sits with the Global Health Engineering Open Science Team, which already runs ORD, RDM, FAIR and AI training as standing activities. Sustainability has two parts. The assets are Open Educational Resources: templates, slides, websites, and an instructor handbook, following the pattern already proven with the Git for Scientists material published through the DSN, and Adriana Clavijo Daza is a certified Carpentries instructor. The competencies travel through the groups participants return to, carried by the data management strategy each participant drafts for their own group. For the FAIR Coalition, the programme is a mechanism to bring more ETH researchers to sign the Charter. The funding model is the per-participant fee: this grant funds and tests the first cohort at CHF 2,000 per place, and later cohorts can fund delivery through the same fee, potentially cross-subsidised through the Coalition.
rationale: Cut the sentence about colleagues noticing, which is a prediction rather than a commitment.

shortened: The project contributes to both communities the call names. Adriana Clavijo Daza is a DSN member, the applicants will sign the FAIR Coalition Charter, and the programme feeds its materials, workflow, and lessons on community-specific FAIR practice back into the DSN, while giving the ETH Library a practical test of the ETH RDM guidelines against real researcher data. The link to the Research Software Engineering community runs through the RSE Network channel, used for recruitment and for sharing results. Lars Schöbitz has proposed a talk to the EnhanceR Symposium 2026 on the approach this programme scales, teaching Git, version control, and coding agents to researchers who do not come from IT, and will deepen that engagement with those responsible for teaching and training at ETH Scientific IT Services.
rationale: Merged the Library sentence into the DSN one and joined the closing two sentences.
